subject.title: refactor(auth): harden CLI forwarding proposal boundary

question: Should credential-derived CLI preparation remain a narrow backend-owned `prepareExecution` capability, or should OpenClaw replace the private Gemini bridge with a generic provider-owned forwarding API?
rationale: The branch proves a validator can be written safely in isolation, but only maintainers can choose the permanent plugin/auth ownership boundary and authorize a new compatibility-sensitive API.

options.title: Harden the existing backend hook
options.body: Keep `prepareExecution` canonical and minimize the concrete bundled Gemini input and result without adding a parallel provider API.

options.title: Sponsor an atomic generic migration
options.body: Add the generic contract only together with its runtime consumer, removal of the private credential branch, SDK baseline, documentation, and live upgrade/security proof.

options.title: Close the unused proposal
options.body: Close this draft if no concrete consumer requires a capability that the existing backend hook cannot express.

recommendation.title: Harden the existing backend hook
recommendation.body: Keep `prepareExecution` canonical and minimize the concrete bundled Gemini input and result without adding a parallel provider API.

likelyOwner.reason: His recent work defines the current canonical CLI execution bridge and its ownership comments, making him the best available owner for deciding whether that seam should be evolved or replaced.
